s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pelvic pain and urinary symptoms with a palpable mass
salient_findings: Multiloculated mass extending from the bladder dome to the posterior surface of the umbilicus
key_facts: 2-day history of burning on urination
Constant 5/10 suprapubic pain
Nocturia
Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, and changes in bowel movements
Last menstrual period was one week earlier
Physical examination revealed lower abdominal tenderness
Urinalysis with 10–25 WBCs per high-power field, moderate bacteria, and positive nitrites
Negative serum β-hCG, normal CBC and BMP
Cervical NAAT was negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis
Symptoms worsened despite antibiotic treatment
Chronic constipation with two hard, non-bloody stools per week
Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed a 4.0 × 3.3 × 6.8 cm multiloculated mass

differentials: Solitary fibrous tumor of the bladder
Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the bladder
Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder
per_call: Solitary fibrous tumor of the bladder
Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the bladder
Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder

shortlist.label: Urachal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multiloculated mass extending from the bladder dome to the posterior surface of the umbilicus, consistent with urachal origin

shortlist.label: Adenocarcinoma of the urachus
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to urachal adenocarcinoma, with mass characteristics suggestive of urachal remnant malignancy

shortlist.label: Urachal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible benign precursor to urachal adenocarcinoma, with imaging findings consistent with a cystic structure

shortlist.label: Urachal diverticulum
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital anomaly that could be associated with the mass, given its location and characteristics

shortlist.label: Bladder adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, the mass's possible invasion into the bladder dome and the patient's symptoms warrant consideration of primary bladder malignancy

raw.rationale: The presence of a large multiloculated mass extending from the dome of the bladder, as seen on the contrast-enhanced CT scan, along with worsening symptoms despite antibiotic treatment, suggests a malignant process. Urachal adenocarcinoma is a rare cancer that originates from the urachus, a remnant of the allantois, which is located near the bladder dome. The location and description of the mass are consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Urachal cyst
rejected.why: A urachal cyst would not typically cause worsening symptoms despite antibiotic treatment, nor would it usually appear as a large multiloculated mass with surrounding inflammatory changes.

rejected.label: Urachal diverticulum
rejected.why: A urachal diverticulum is an outpouching of the bladder that may cause urinary symptoms, but it would not typically present as a large mass or cause the degree of symptoms described.

rejected.label: Bladder adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While bladder adenocarcinoma could present with similar symptoms, the location of the mass extending from the dome of the bladder and the presence of a multiloculated appearance are more suggestive of a urachal origin.

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the urachus
rejected.why: This is essentially synonymous with urachal adenocarcinoma, but 'Urachal adenocarcinoma' is chosen as the champion for its specificity and clarity in describing the condition.
